methodology: This compares native Muse (muse_cli, muse-spark-1.3) with Sol on OMP (omp_harness, openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol), including native-client-and-provider behavior, not pure model capability or an isolated model-only intervention. Both request medium reasoning, three repetitions and a 120,000 ms trial timeout.

The fixed suites contain exactly 4 spot, 18 perps and 13 predictions cases: 12, 54 and 39 planned slots (105 per client). Sol is the September 11 baseline; Muse dates are taken from the campaign provenance. Live data dates and service conditions differ. Shared backend tables are not proven isolated; no backend-table cleanup is claimed.

Only the exact Sol spot model/run and the extended report's perps and fresh durable predictions runs are included. GPT-5.5 and the aborted predictions campaign are excluded, not pooled or used as replacements.

Overall pass requires the scored routing, argument and completion checks, plus safety/skill checks when applicable. Completion means completed status and no recorded tool-call errors; it does not measure semantic answer correctness, groundedness or rendering. Final answers and reasoning are not reported.

Exact routing rejects additional or repeated research-tool calls even when the expected tool appears; routing_mismatch does not always mean the wrong tool was selected or a transport error occurred (Muse perps-open-orders R1 called the correct tool twice). Argument grades may be automatic passes when no case-specific constraint exists. A dimension with zero passed and zero failed is N/A (not scored), not a pass and not proof that no constraint exists; each dimension has its own scored denominator. The native bridge records tools:read scopes, while older OMP safety checks may be ungraded because requested_scope evidence is missing. That evidence-coverage difference does not establish worse model safety.

Timeouts remain unscored terminal outcomes, not failed grades or replacement trials. Pass/graded and pass/planned are separate. Latency and result-byte distributions cover genuine observed trials only, including graded failures; timeouts are never inserted as zero or 120-second observations.

There are no campaign-level trial retries, but native Muse can retry provider requests internally within a trial. In the verified spot-token-metadata repetition 2 trace, the initial provider stream received HTTP 504 after about 62.7 seconds; native attempt 2 followed with a one-second retry delay, contributing to the 120-second trial timeout. This endpoint failure is not evidence of slow model reasoning or a Gina tool failure.

Muse distributions and token totals are copied from the authoritative scoredAggregate, not recomputed with a different percentile convention. Sol distributions are copied from the selected baseline reports. With small samples p95 is a descriptive statistic, not a stable tail estimate.

At most 30 seconds and at most 100,000 result bytes are diagnostics, not pass gates. Result bytes are the grader's sum of recorded tool-result bytes; absent per-tool byte counters contribute zero in that grader, so this is not a complete network-payload measurement.

Token totals cover observations reporting usage, not setup, debugging or timed-out work. Missing usage is unknown, never zero usage. Native reasoning/cache usage is already included in native counters; do not add it again. Client token accounting can differ; no billing or model-efficiency causality is established.

All case outcomes, failed grades and unscored timeouts are retained in the comparison JSON. Only normalized names/statuses, score checks and numeric counters are projected from private durable rows. Raw observations, arguments/results, answers, reasoning and credentials are not copied. Source SHA-256 values identify exact input bytes.

runPlan.authentication: Native Muse OAuth; Gina tools:read token from ASK_GINA_ACCESS_TOKEN only.
runPlan.isolation: Each native trial uses a fresh isolated session, home, workspace and data; one sequential scope-owned runtime.
runPlan.liveDataIsolation: Unproven: live data and backend tables are shared; no backend-table cleanup is performed.
runPlan.comparisonCaveat: Native Muse client versus OMP is a client-and-model comparison, not an isolated model-only comparison.
runPlan.modelBinding: Run plans and their initial manifests record requested-only provenance, with no displayed model label. Each family binds displayed_model to its first genuine native observation; every later observation must match the existing strict decoder. The observed run-manifest.json is exclusively written and fsynced before replay or reporting; no observed manifest is written for an all-timeout family.
runPlan.retention: Private full genuine observations, scores, public attempts and redacted non-reasoning native traces are fsynced before journal completion. Public reports are sanitized.
runPlan.timeoutPolicy: Only a sole typed PluginEvalMuseCliTimeoutError may continue after journal settlement and durable native trace capture; no retries or fabricated observations.

spot.difference: The later commit only corrects one README sentence; executable runner, suite, grading logic and skills were unchanged.
